relevance_note: The paper describes 23 individually named patients with enzyme-confirmed (or, for one, deduced) SSADH deficiency ("case reports of 23 new patients"); no ALDH5A1 variant is reported for anyone, so the variants table is empty.
method_note: Built with a Python script from my reading of the paper; Table cells were sliced by column from the Markdown rows and checked by eye against the Table. The paper is an OCR of the publisher PDF. The clinical Table is split in two parts. Part 1 columns: Patient | Sex | Age at Diagnosis | Ethnicity | Consanguinity | Neonatal Problems | Normal Early Development | Mental Delay | Motor Delay | Language Delay | Ataxia | Hypotonia. Part 2 columns: Patient | Reflexes | Ocular Problems | Behavioral Problems | Hyperkinesis | Psychosis | Seizures | Electroencephalogram | Neuroimaging | Carnitine | Treatment with Vigabatrin. Part 2 rows 'B.H. C.S.' and 'P.V.l TA.' merge two patients each, so none of their cells were used for anyone (B.H., C.S., P.V., T.A. part-2 data come from the case reports only). Garbled or stacked cells were not used: '+ / -' (J.E.Y., P.F. hypotonia; N.O. ataxia), 'n', '+ t + t' (P.V. motor), '+ + / - §' (D.E. seizures), '+±' (E.G. seizures), 'I' (I.C. seizures), '4-', '-f-', '- #iii 11', '- -', '+ +', 'Abnormal Abnormal', 'MRI normal CT normal' (P.S. row), 'MRI probably normal?'. The legend does not define '-', so '-' cells are not reported; '+' cells were read as observed, and word cells (Normal, Abnormal, Absent, Decreased, Low) were used. 'Normal Early Development' '+' is recorded as excluded 'early developmental delay'. Checklist mapping: Mental Delay -> intellectual disability, Motor Delay -> motor deficits, Language Delay -> speech/language; Hyperkinesis/hyperactivity mapped to attention problems only when the text also names poor concentration or attention. Normal brain MRI/CT is recorded as excluded 'abnormal brain MRI/CT' only; checklist T2 and atrophy items left not reported for those people. N.O. 'hyperintensive signals in the area of the left globus pallidus' (MRI; T2 not stated) was mapped to the T2 item; K.S. 'symmetric lesions in the globus pallidus' was not (no signal stated). Contradiction: A.F. text 'electroencephalographic background was diffusely slow' vs Table EEG 'Normal' (possibly OCR column shift); both rows emitted, checklist EEG item not reported. Changes over time not treated as contradictions: M.S. normal tone at one examination, later hypotonic (Table: 'Developed later'); P.L. hypotonia resolved at 13 months on vigabatrin; M.H. areflexia at 4 months, normal deep-tendon reflexes at 16 months; B.H. 'MRI showed no abnormalities and a minor increase in signal' (only the signal finding recorded). Hedged statements not recorded as features: D.E. 'may have had a few very short astatic seizures'; T.A. CT 'raised the question of cerebellar atrophy'. Y.A. seizures rest only on Table '+§'; the text describes febrile episodes of clouded consciousness and an EEG with no epileptic abnormalities. No ALDH5A1 variant or molecular analysis is reported for anyone (authors: 'until we have determined through molecular analysis that the disease maps to this locus in each patient'), so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null; cohort_size_as_stated is 23. Diagnosis basis comes from the Methods statement covering 'all patients (except P.S.H.)'; P.S.H. was diagnosed by deduction after death. OCR-garbled ages (e.g. '3V2 y', '9lA y', '6% y', '4 ]/2 y', '7Vz years', '13!/2 years') are copied verbatim with ISO left null; P.S.H. deceased age left null for the same reason. Labels use the paper's initials in their most frequent form; OCR variants in headings or table ('I .O .', 'LO.', 'ICS.', 'JXY.', 'J.LY.1I', 'U S ,', 'i.e.', 'TA .') were normalized to I.O., K.S., J.I.Y., M.S., I.C., T.A. No family labels are printed. Relationships: A.E.-M. and M.H. are first cousins; J.E.Y. and J.I.Y. are sisters; P.S.H., P.S. and P.V. are sisters. Relatives given rows: I.C.'s 'maternal sister' (hydrocephalus, developmental delay, died at 33) and 'paternal cousin' (developmental delay), and P.S.H.'s mother (atactic gait). Healthy, untested siblings of B.H., I.O., K.S., M.H., M.S. and T.A. are out of scope and got no rows. N.O. was previously reported (ref. 6). Treatment effects are recorded only in treatment_summary, apart from adverse effects (I.O. agitation, N.O. seizures, P.S. hypersalivation and sleepiness), which are features with the drug noted in severity_or_detail.
